lines: A formant vocal synthesiser: a glottal source through three band-pass filters that morph across the vowels OO, OH, AH, AY and EE, followed by a stereo ping-pong delay
Sets the pitch in volts at one volt per octave, 0V to 10V, with 5V giving C4 at 261.63Hz
Sets the level of the synthesised voice going into the delay and the outputs, 0 to 100%
A latch putting the voice under gate control; unlit, the voice sounds without stopping, and lit, the voice sounds only while GATE is above 1V or a MIDI note is held
Sweeps the three formant frequencies across the five vowels in order, OO at the left through OH, AH and AY to EE at the right
Sets how long the pitch takes to slide to a new value, 0 to 5 seconds
Sets the depth of a 5.5Hz vibrato on the pitch, reaching one semitone either way at the clockwise end
Scales all three formant frequencies together, 0.85 times at the left to 1.15 times at the right, which shifts the whole vowel up or down without changing the pitch
Scales the voltage at VOWEL CV, -100% to +100%, before it is added to the VOWEL knob; at the centre that jack changes nothing
Adds to the GLIDE time, 10V adding 5 seconds, and the total is held between 0 and 5 seconds
Adds to the VIBRATO depth, 10V covering the whole depth, and the total is held between none and full
Adds to the FORMANT scaling, 10V covering the whole span between 0.85 times and 1.15 times, and the total is held inside it
Moves the vowel, scaled by VOW ATT; at a full attenuverter 10V covers the whole sweep from OO to EE, and the total with the knob is held inside it
Adds to the PITCH knob at one volt per octave
Adds to the VOICE level, 10V covering the whole range, and the total is held between silence and full
While GATE ON is lit the voice sounds whenever the voltage here is above 1V and fades out when it falls; with GATE ON unlit this jack is not read at all
Each rise above 1V flips the GATE ON latch, so a trigger here does what pressing that button does
Sets the delay time, 10ms at the left to 2 seconds at the right; with a clock at SYNC DELAY it instead picks which whole multiple of the clock period the delay takes
Sets how much of each delayed channel is fed back into the other one, 0 to 100%
Balances the dry signal against the delayed one, dry alone at the left and delay alone at the right
Sets how much of the signal at EXT IN is added to the voice before the delay, 0 to 100%
Adds to the TIME knob, 10V covering the whole sweep between 10ms and 2 seconds, and the total is held inside it
An audio signal to run through the delay alongside the voice, scaled by INPUT MIX before it is added
Adds to the MIX balance, 10V covering the whole span from dry to delay, and the total is held inside it
Adds to the INPUT MIX level, 10V covering the whole span, and the total is held between 0 and 100%
A clock here is timed from one rise above 1V to the next, and the delay time is snapped to a whole multiple of that period, with TIME choosing the multiple
The voice's pitch in volts at one volt per octave, taken after the glide and without the vibrato
The left channel of the dry signal mixed with the delay, soft-clipped through a tanh so it stops short of ±10V
The right channel of the dry signal mixed with the delay, soft-clipped through a tanh so it stops short of ±10V
Note — the voice sounds from the moment the module is placed and keeps sounding; press GATE ON to make it answer a gate instead
Note — the delay crosses over between the channels, each side fed from the other side's delayed signal, so the repeats alternate between the two outputs
Note — a MIDI note sets the pitch and restarts the glottal cycle, and while any note is held the voice counts as gated
Note — MIDI pitch bend sweeps the vowel, the mod wheel adds vibrato depth, CC12 moves the delay mix and CC13 moves the formant scaling
Note — the pitch wanders very slightly on its own, from a slow random jitter mixed in before the glide, and that jitter is carried on PITCH OUT
Menu — MIDI driver — picks which MIDI system the module takes its notes from
Menu — MIDI device — picks which attached MIDI device feeds the module
Menu — MIDI channel — picks which MIDI channel is read, or all of them

VocalLamma.notes: Read from the maker's source at commit 6651d58, the only commit whose plugin.json carries the installed 2.2.0, and that file is byte-identical to the installed one. Every control and jack has a widget, so all of them are covered. The manual disagrees with the code in two places. It says polyphonic cables can carry mults to LEFT and RIGHT: both outputs are written with a plain setVoltage and no setChannels, so they are mono. And it gives the delay buffer as about 22.8 seconds at 48kHz, where the buffer is 2 to the 19th samples, which is 10.9 seconds at that rate; the knob's own 10ms to 2 second range is what a reader meets either way, so no buffer figure is quoted in the lines. The manual also describes the pitch jitter as about 0.08 semitones; the code adds it in volts, so the scale factor is 0.08 of an octave, though the jitter itself is smoothed so heavily that the audible wander is far smaller than either figure, and no number for it is quoted. FEEDBACK is the one delay knob with no CV jack. The MIDI menu items are Rack's own, named from the application's English translation file.
